messages:
maya_r: ran an nsys capture on the KV-prefetch + batching repro (attached: /artifacts/nsys/1765439876-repro.qdrep). timeline looks weird — large host->device memcpy blocks that appear to be serializing with kernels instead of overlapping.

alex_k: are those cudaMemcpyAsync calls or plain cudaMemcpy?

maya_r: they come from the prefetch path. code is currently using std::vector + cudaMemcpy (host pageable) in the batcher before enqueueing. i think we accidentally fell back to blocking copies on default stream.

simon_t: that would do it. pageable host mem -> blocking copy that runs on default stream will serialize kernels. also saw CPU gaps in the trace around the batcher thread: ~40-120ms where nothing is scheduled on the host thread between enqueues. could be sleeping on a condvar or getting preempted.

jamie_ops: do we have NVTX markers around prefetch/copy? makes it 10x easier to map timeline to code.

maya_r: not yet — forgot to add them. i captured with --trace=cuda,osrt and the raw timeline is attached. here's the command i used:

```
nsys profile --output 1765439876 --trace=cuda,osrt --sample=cpu --capture-range=nvtx
```

perf-bot: suggestion: include --capture-range=cpu to correlate host gaps, and add --sample=none if you want full resolution of short kernels. also try --stop-on-exit to keep qdrep small. :robot_face: 

alex_k: quick wins: 1) switch prefetch buffers to cudaHostAlloc (pinned) + cudaMemcpyAsync into a dedicated stream -> should use copy engine and overlap with kernels 2) reuse pinned buffers to avoid repeated host allocations 3) mark NVTX around prefetch, enqueue, and postprocess.

maya_r: agree. other observation: kernel selection for short sequences is currently emitting many tiny kernels (dispatcher overhead). when memcpys are blocking we see those tiny kernels pushed later, increasing total tail latency. maybe pick fused kernels for small seq lengths.

simon_t: also check which stream the KV cache prefetch is using — if prefetch and subsequent KV writes run on the same stream as inference kernels we won't get overlap. run `nsys stats` to see per-stream timing or open the timeline and filter by stream.

jamie_ops: action items:
- maya: add NVTX around prefetch/copy, switch to pinned+Async for a quick experiment (try single dedicated stream for copies)
- alex: try kernel-selection tweak to reduce tiny-kernel count for seq<=32 and run perf baseline
- simon: produce a short instr for how to interpret copy-engine vs generic memcpy on the nsys timeline (screenshot + example)

perf-bot: recommended capture flags to reproduce overlap detail:

```
nsys profile --output 1765439876-followup --trace=cuda,osrt,osrt:stack --sample=none --capture-range=nvtx --force-overwrite
```

maya_r: i'll spin up a branch today. my hunch: pageable->blocking copies + batcher host-thread gaps are compounding to create long tail. if pinned+async + reuse solves overlap, then next we iterate on batching heuristic to avoid bursts of huge memcpy windows that starve the copy engine.

alex_k: cool. if pinned helps, we should add an allocator behind the batcher and guardrails so user-level code can't accidentally pass pageable containers.

simon_t: and if CPU gaps persist, instrument the batcher condvar/wakeup path — maybe switch to eventfd or reduce sleep backoff. those 50-100ms gaps are big enough to explain latency spikes.

jamie_ops: created task INF-1245 with the repro and assigned to maya/alex/simon. tag me on the PR and i'll pull a fresh capture in CI. :white_check_mark:
